flagged.evidence: Fact [L5] says the Dirac evaluation identity “is proved locally in step 1.1.” But Step 1.1 invokes [L5] to evaluate the integral of |h-s| as zero, in order to establish that s is an admissible approximant. This uses the identity being proved; checking directly from the Dirac mass would close the small gap.

The page says the Poisson extension remains bounded below “along a tangential curve approaching 1.” The cited counterexample establishes u(z_n) ≥ (π+1)⁻² at discrete points z_n and that their approach is tangential; it gives no continuous curve or lower bound between those points. The sequence witness does not license the stronger curve claim.

Step 4.1 defines Î_i = {η : d(c_i,η) < 3h_i} and says it “is T when 3h_i ≥ 1/2.” At equality, the antipode has distance exactly 1/2 and is excluded, so Î_i is T minus that point. Its measure is still 1, and the later estimate remains valid.
